title: How to Get BIR Authority to Print (Invoices)
description: Apply for the mandatory Authority to Print (ATP) for your business invoices and receipts under the Ease of Paying Taxes Act.

requirements.title: BIR Form 1906
requirements.description: The application form for Authority to Print.

requirements.title: BIR COR (Form 2303)
requirements.description: A photocopy of your BIR Certificate of Registration.

requirements.title: Sample Layout
requirements.description: A draft of your proposed invoice showing all mandatory business information.

requirements.title: Accredited Printer
requirements.description: Details of a BIR-authorized printing shop for your booklets.

checklist.title: Find Printer

checklist.title: Create Layout
checklist.description: Work with the printer to design an invoice layout that complies with EOPT rules.

checklist.description: Submit your ATP application through the ORUS portal or your assigned RDO.

checklist.description: Get the official Authority to Print (Form 1921) from the BIR once approved.

checklist.description: Collect your printed invoice booklets once the printer has completed the job.

content.title: What is the Authority to Print (ATP)?

blocks.content: The **Authority to Print (ATP)** is a permit issued by the BIR that allows a business to print its own official Invoices and Receipts through an accredited printer.

**Note for 2026:** Under the **Ease of Paying Taxes (EOPT) Act**, the **"Invoice"** is now the primary document for both sales of goods and services. The traditional "Official Receipt" is now a supplementary document.

The ATP and Invoices are commonly used for:
*   Issuing legal proof of sale to customers
*   Claiming Input VAT (for VAT-registered buyers)
*   Substantiating business income and expenses during audits

You may need an ATP if you are:
- A new business owner (Sole Proprietor or Corporation)
- A freelancer or self-employed professional
- An existing business whose current invoice booklets are running out
- An existing business transitioning from "Official Receipts" to "Invoices" under the new law
Official invoices are the backbone of a legal business in the Philippines.

blocks.title: Professionalism and Trust
blocks.content: Issuing a BIR-registered invoice builds trust with corporate clients who need these documents for their own tax deductions.

blocks.title: Avoidance of Penalties
blocks.content: Failure to issue an official invoice for sales can result in fines starting at ₱10,000 per violation.

blocks.title: Online (ORUS)
blocks.content: You can apply for the ATP digitally via the [BIR ORUS Portal](https://orus.bir.gov.ph).

blocks.title: Walk-In (RDO)
blocks.content: Submit your Form 1906 and requirements to the Revenue District Office (RDO) where your business is registered.
**Pro Tip:** Use the BIR **eFPS or eBIRForms** for faster filing and avoid manual queuing at the RDO. Most payments can now be done via GCash or Maya.

blocks.title: Find an Accredited Printer
blocks.content: Look for a printer with a "BIR Accredited" sign. Request a quote for printing (usually sold in sets of 10 or 50 booklets).

blocks.title: Create the Layout
blocks.content:
Work with the printer to create your invoice layout. Ensure it includes:
*   "Invoice" title (not "Official Receipt")
*   Your Business Name, Address, and TIN (with Branch Code)
*   Space for Customer Name, Address, and TIN
*   VAT breakdown (if applicable)

blocks.title: File BIR Form 1906
blocks.content: Log in to **ORUS** or visit your **RDO**. Submit the application and upload/attach the sample layout and your COR.

blocks.title: Receive the ATP (Form 1921)
blocks.content: Once approved, the BIR will issue the **Authority to Print (Form 1921)**.

blocks.title: Printing and Delivery
blocks.content: Give the ATP to your printer. They will print your booklets and must submit a **Printer’s Certificate of Delivery (PCD)** to the BIR within 30 days. You can then pick up your official booklets.

Applicants may process their ATP at:
- [BIR ORUS Portal](https://orus.bir.gov.ph)
- Your assigned **Revenue District Office (RDO)**

Typical processing timelines include:
*   ATP Approval: 1–3 Working Days
*   Printing Duration: 1–2 Weeks (depends on the printer)
If applying via ORUS, you can check the "Application Status" tab in your dashboard. If manual, you will need to follow up with your RDO or the printer.

Applicants may experience:
- **Layout Rejection:** If mandatory information is missing or the text is too small.
- **Printer Delay:** Printers may have a backlog, especially during peak registration seasons (January).

items: **Using "Official Receipt" for Services:** Ensure your new booklets say **"Invoice"** to comply with 2026 EOPT rules.
**Printing without ATP:** Never print receipts or invoices through a non-accredited shop; they will not be legally valid.

blocks.content: Always check the serial numbers on your printed booklets against the ATP to ensure they match.

items: Ask your printer if they can handle the BIR filing for you.
Ensure your COR is updated and shows the correct "Registered Activity."
Print at least 10–20 booklets at once to save on the per-unit cost.

blocks.content:
For the most accurate and up-to-date information, please refer to:
*   [Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR)](https://www.bir.gov.ph)
*   [BIR Online Registration and Update System (ORUS)](https://orus.bir.gov.ph)

blocks.title: Can I use generic "Receipt" booklets from bookstores?
blocks.content: No. For a registered business, only invoices/receipts printed with an official ATP and serial numbers are valid for tax purposes.

blocks.title: Do Invoices expire?
blocks.content: Invoices no longer have a 5-year expiration date (as of RR 6-2022). You can use them until the booklets are consumed.
